To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the slope of the activation functions near origin is an important factor for training deep networks, 2) the logistic sigmoid can be improved to be as effective as the tanh, and 3) the penalized tanh is comparable and even superior to the ReLU and leak ReLU on deep networks.

(1) we show that the logistic function is a good alternative to tanh, and (2) we show that penalized tanh is a good alternative and even outperformed the state-of-the-arts non-saturated activation functions.
the logistic function can be made to behave more like tanh by rescaling, and that the tanh function can be improved by penalizing in its negative part.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in addition to non-zero centered property of activation functions, their slope near the origin also plays a critical role in training deep networks.

we show that the saturation property is not the only problem in training deep networks, and we provide some evidence that the slow convergence in deep learning may be due to the non-smoothness and non-zero centered property of the activation functions.
, in deep architectures, activation function is not only a nonlinear transformation but also a weight regularization.

the slope of the activation functions at the origin should also be considered as a design criteria when selecting the activation function for a deep network.
